A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same cross-model bias study. Their text, equations, tables, figures and appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial retitling and reorganization.

before.justification: v3 reports original BBQ and UnQover evaluations, representation comparisons, and StereoSet sentiment and generation-failure results in Appendix G.

after.justification: v4 reports results for an expanded model set and retains original CKA and StereoSet experiments, including the generation analysis in Appendix H.

M1.justification: BSM names and organizes the existing accuracy, bias-score, histogram, cosine-distance, UNK-flip and CKA analyses. No operational algorithm change or new training component is established. JSD and sentiment analysis already appeared in v3.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate BBQ, UnQover and reformatted StereoSet, retaining the same demographic coverage and English QA and completion tasks. Code, multilingual and multimodal extensions in v4 are proposed applications, not evaluated coverage.

E2.justification: The comparative audit adds LLaMA 3.1 8B/70B and LLaMA 3.2 3B base/chat variants, plus GPT-5-mini, substantially extending release and proprietary-model comparisons. Alpaca disappears from updated accuracy and distance plots but remains in the bias-score table. CKA and StereoSet comparator sets are retained.

E3.justification: v4 introduces 3B evaluation configurations and explicitly excludes the newly added GPT-5-mini from UnQover. The reported UnQover size changes from approximately 1M samples per dimension to approximately 1M overall, without establishing resampling. Existing BBQ sample totals and the 2,106-prompt greedy StereoSet protocol remain.

E4.justification: The base-versus-tuned analysis extends to LLaMA 3.1/3.2, adding evidence on generational differences and small-model bias increases despite increased abstention. This extends an existing analytical question; the CKA, metric-comparison and StereoSet failure analyses are largely retained.

E5.justification: Neither version supplies repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. v4 states that uncertainty is reported for within-family deltas, but provides no corresponding estimation procedure or uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: v4 adds substantial model-level results and revises existing accuracy outcomes: GPT-4o-mini, labeled gpt4 in v3 Figure 1, changes from strongly uneven to consistently high accuracy in v4 Figure 2. The PDFs do not explain these revisions. LLaMA 3 70B's mean s_AMB changes from -1.92 to -1.42; shared detailed bias, flip, CKA and StereoSet results are largely retained.

T1.justification: v4 Section 3.1 introduces a formal six-component pairwise bias-similarity signature S(Mi, Mj | X, D). This is a limited mathematical formalization, without new theorems or proofs. The bias-score equations are retained, and the explicit UNK-flip formula restates the earlier verbal definition.

C1.justification: v4 elevates the descriptive study into a claimed unified BSM framework enabling procurement, fairness-drift audits and lineage screening. It adds headline claims about small-model tuning failures, cost advantages and extensibility beyond language benchmarks, substantially expanding the claimed contribution.

C2.justification: v4 develops new family-generation interpretations, selective-abstention explanations for small-model bias increases, homogenization risks and procurement recommendations. It also explicitly limits cross-vendor comparisons to observational interpretation and adds cost and API-access limitations. These extend the earlier discussion beyond merely relocating its limitations.

D1.justification: v4 adds a code-access link, specifies that cosine distance uses raw count vectors without normalization, and documents GPT-5-mini's cost-related exclusion from UnQover. These improve disclosure without establishing corresponding changes to the underlying implementation.

R1.justification: Section 2 substantially updates research positioning through CEB, BEATS, FairMT-Bench, counterfactual-bias certification, the 50-plus-model implicit-bias study and an explicit contrast with Polyrating. It strengthens the claimed distinction between BSM and prior evaluation approaches; publication-metadata updates alone are not counted.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, methodology narrative and discussion are extensively rewritten around BSM. Evaluation setup becomes a separate section, discussion and conclusion are merged, and limitations and societal impacts move into reorganized appendices.

P2.justification: v4 adopts a single-column conference layout, adds a pipeline diagram, a joint flip/bias visualization and a qualitative summary table. Main-text cosine panels give way to appendix displays, the mean-CKA heatmap is replaced by a table, and enlarged histograms are split and rotated. Retained appendix CKA heatmaps are unchanged.

improvement.justification: v4 broadens the comparative evidence and improves access information and causal-scope qualifications. However, its new Table 1 reports Gemma 3 4B's average s_DIS as 2.69, while the retained dimension-level values in Table 5 average approximately -5.35. Procurement and cost recommendations also lack a clearly specified supporting evaluation, and substantial accuracy revisions remain unexplained. These reliability problems make the net benefit of the useful additions uncertain.
